title: Subtype Mixing via Shared Struct Fields
damaged_code:
```rust
struct Bicycle {
    is_mountain: bool,
    is_recumbent: bool,
    suspension_travel: Option<f64>,
    seat_angle: Option<f64>,
}
```
pattern: Representing distinct concrete subtypes by merging their separate field attributes together under a single type using conditional flags.
why_bad: It prevents extending the system when a new type represents a mixture of existing types (e.g., a recumbent mountain bike). It forces developers to write complex conditional checks inside every operation, leading to fragile state mutations.
detection: A single class/struct containing multiple optional fields that are only ever valid under mutually exclusive boolean flags.
counterexample: Standard Option fields representing independent, non-exclusionary attributes (e.g., an optional nickname).
source: Sandi Metz *POODR*, Chapter 7: "Insist on the Abstraction", p. 158, 197.
